title: Map of slices: positions and invert
hints: Start each result with an empty literal: `out := map[string][]int{}` / `map[int][]string{}`. A missing key reads as a nil slice, and `append` on a nil slice allocates one.
`Positions`: `for i, w := range words { pos[w] = append(pos[w], i) }`. Indices come out increasing because you walk the slice in order. `Invert`: `for k, v := range m { out[v] = append(out[v], k) }`.

Map order is random, so sort `Invert`'s groups afterwards: `for _, keys := range out { slices.Sort(keys) }`. Sorting in place works because each value shares its backing array with the slice stored in the map.
